before:
Kiln Room - Firing Queue Settings

The shared kiln at the riverside pottery annexe runs two loads a week, and the queue is filled by the technician each Thursday evening. When more work is submitted than the chamber will hold, glaze firings are placed ahead of bisque firings, and bisque firings ahead of test tiles. Everything submitted stays eligible for a slot; nothing is refused on grounds of category, and members may still withdraw a piece up to noon on Friday. The technician notes the loaded order in the wall book so that anyone arriving later can see where their work sits. Unfired work carries forward to the following week without losing its place in the sequence.

before:
Chandlery Store - Issuing Paint from the Locked Cabinet

Two-pack paint and its hardener are held in the yellow cabinet at the back of the chandlery store. Anyone drawing stock signs the tally sheet with the tin size and the date. The store hand may issue paint to a member without a supervisor present, provided the tally sheet is completed before the tin leaves the room. Part-used tins come back the same afternoon so that the cabinet is shut by four o'clock, when the yard alarm is set. Spills are wiped with the rags in the blue bin, which the yard contractor empties on Wednesdays. The cabinet key hangs on the hook behind the counter door.

before:
Burial Ground Register - Enquiry Responses

The parish clerk keeps the register of interments and answers enquiries from families tracing relatives. Where a plot number cannot be matched to the name supplied, the standing reply reads: "We regret that no corresponding entry can be located in the volumes held at this office." The clerk then lists the volumes searched and the years covered, and invites the enquirer to supply any variant spelling. A copy of each reply is filed with the original letter in the enquiry box. Replies go out within ten working days. The register itself is not amended in consequence of an enquiry; corrections follow the separate route through the burial committee.

before:
Allotment Site Committee - Minutes, Item 4

The committee considered the fenced ground between plot 22 and the water trough, which has been mown but not cultivated for three seasons. The secretary reported that the ground stands on the site plan as a vacant plot, and that the figures returned to the council each March are drawn from that plan. Two members observed that the surface is compacted and that the hedge on its north side has been left to grow out. The treasurer noted that no rent has been collected against it. It was agreed the entry would be settled before the next return was prepared, and the secretary would amend the plan accordingly.

before:
Tide Gauge Manual - Section 6: Reading the Stilling Well

The float sits in a stilling well of 150 mm bore, and the tape is read against the brass index at the top of the housing. Readings taken during heavy swell are affected by drawdown at the inlet, and the observed level is understood to sit some 20 mm below the true still-water level in those conditions. Observers should note the sea state alongside each reading so the office can apply the correction. The gauge is checked against the staff on the outer wall each quarter. Do not adjust the index screw; report any discrepancy greater than 5 mm to the harbour office in writing.

before:
Reserve Bulletin - Spring Wader Counts

The volunteer count on the east scrape logged 46 lapwing on the morning of 12 March, with lower numbers on the two following visits. Water levels were held high through February and the islands stayed partly submerged until the sluice was opened. Counters work from the north hide between seven and nine o'clock and hand their sheets to the warden's tray at the visitor barn. Anyone unable to attend should tell the rota keeper the evening before so a stand-in can be found. The bulletin is printed monthly and left in the barn; a copy also goes to the grazing tenant, who asks to be told when the sluice is next opened.

before:
Notice to Bellringers - Tower Opening

Ringers arriving first should work through the steps posted by the door. Unlock the vestry gate, switch on the stair light, raise the sound shutters, and then untie the ropes at the sallies. The tower captain checks the shutters before ringing begins. Nothing may be rung before the shutters are up, and the stair light stays on until the last person leaves. Practice runs from half past seven until nine. Visitors sign the book on the ledge. On leaving, the steps are worked in reverse, and the vestry gate is padlocked. Any fault with the shutter cords is written in the tower book for the steeple keeper.

before:
Boat Club Handbook - Winter Storage Charges

Craft laid up in the compound are charged for the storage season, and the charge for each craft is worked out from its overall length multiplied by the yard's standing rate for the season. The steward measures each hull on arrival and enters the figure on the storage card. Payment falls due within fourteen days of the card being issued. Trailers left alongside a cradle are charged at the flat trailer rate. Craft taken away before the end of February are not refunded. The compound gate code changes each October and is sent out with the storage card. Uncollected craft after May are dealt with under the lien notice at the gate.
after:
Boat Club Handbook - Winter Storage Charges

Craft laid up in the compound are charged for the storage season, and the charge for each craft is worked out from the deck area enclosed by its overall length and beam, at the yard's standing rate per square metre. The steward measures each hull on arrival and enters the figure on the storage card. Payment falls due within fourteen days of the card being issued. Trailers left alongside a cradle are charged at the flat trailer rate. Craft taken away before the end of February are not refunded. The compound gate code changes each October and is sent out with the storage card. Uncollected craft after May are dealt with under the lien notice at the gate.
variation_site: The first sentence, where the charge for a craft is arrived at.
author_note: Swaps the calculation actually applied to derive the charge; the payment terms and refund conditions stand as they were.

before:
Weighbridge Log - How Entries Are Set Down

Each load crossing the weighbridge is entered by the attendant on the roll sheet. Entries carry ticket number, haulier, gross weight, tare, and time off, separated by commas on a single line, with the date given once at the head of the sheet. The attendant initials the foot of each sheet at the end of the shift and passes it to the yard office, where it is keyed into the returns. Sheets are kept for six years. Where a load is re-weighed, the second entry carries the same ticket number and the note RW after the time. Blank lines are ruled through before the sheet leaves the cabin.

author_note: Changes the delimiter and where the date sits - a human reads the same load, a keying clerk does not.

before:
Village Hall Policy - Who Counts as a Local Hirer

For the purposes of the hire schedule, a local hirer is any individual or group whose registered address lies within the civil parish boundary. Local hirers pay the reduced hourly charge, are exempt from the refundable key deposit, and may book the small room up to twelve months ahead rather than three. The bookings secretary checks the address given on the form against the electoral roll copy held in the office. Regular hirers are re-checked each April. Where a group meets in the hall but is administered elsewhere, the address of the person signing the form is taken. Disputes go to the management committee at its next ordinary meeting.

before:
Footpath Survey Report - Section B, Stiles and Gates

The surveyor walked the eleven paths in the northern half of the parish between April and June. Of the thirty-one stiles inspected, nine were found to be unsound, with rotten treads or missing top rails. Three field gates would not swing clear of the ground. The surveyor photographed each defect and marked its position on the working map, which is lodged with the parish office. Landowners are written to in the order the defects appear on the map, and the county officer is copied in. Work notified as completed is re-inspected in the following season. The survey goes to the council each autumn with the estimated cost of materials.
